documents.title: AI Code of Ethics and Minimum Standards (AI Ethical Considerations and Guidance)
documents.summary: A university-wide AI Council page that sets a short code of ethics and quick tips for teaching, learning, research and work. It asks instructors to state AI expectations in their syllabi and students to cite AI use, but sets no single allow or ban rule. Most content concerns privacy, research practice and staff use.
documents.stance_why: The page says instructors should "Clearly state expectations for AI use in your course syllabus, including what is allowed, what requires disclosure, and what is not permitted", handing the allow-or-ban decision to each course, while students are only told to use AI "in ways that align with Tarleton's academic integrity policies", so the stance is delegates.

units.why: The page states its purpose as guidance for "responsible use of generative AI" campus-wide; this is a statement of purpose and scope, so P56 (institution-wide framework) fits, informs, general.
units.anchor: guidance and recommendations for the responsible use of generative AI

units.why: The goal of harnessing "the benefits of AI" while minimizing risks names benefits of AI for the community; it is a rationale rather than a rule, so P87 fits and P56 does not, because P56 is the framework itself.
units.anchor: harness the benefits of AI while minimizing risks
units.fit_note: Also names risks (academic integrity, privacy, ethics) alongside benefits. Also names the risk areas (academic integrity, privacy, ethical use) the guidance aims to minimize.
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance neutral, B encourage. The sentence states the goal "harness the benefits of AI while minimizing risks"; it is a rationale, not a recommendation to use AI, so neutral. Type P87 agreed.

units.why: "its use must reflect our core values" sets a principle for AI use in academic and operational practice; it is a framework principle (P56) that binds everyone, modality must.
units.anchor: its use must reflect our core values

units.why: The page links TAMUS Regulation 29.01.05 on AI as a governing source; pointing to system regulations fits P77 (existing policy) loosely, informs.
units.anchor: TAMUS Regulation 29.01.05 Artificial Intelligence
units.fit_note: Listed only as a link; the page does not say AI use must comply. Only lists the regulation as a reference link; it does not state a duty in words.

units.why: Warns that "these platforms may use, collect, and store your personal data", a privacy fact motivating caution; P50 (protect personal data) fits, informs.
units.anchor: may use, collect, and store your personal data
units.frag_start: When using an AI tool or

units.why: "it is important to follow data privacy and security guidelines to protect both personal and institutional data" directs protection of data; stated as "important", so should, P50.
units.anchor: follow data privacy and security guidelines to protect both personal and institutional data
units.frag_start: When using generative AI, it is
units.resolution_why: Phase: A during-work, B general. The sentence applies "When using generative AI", i.e. while working with AI tools, so during-work. Modality should and type P50 agreed.

units.why: Under Teach, "Leverage AI to enhance teaching and learning while upholding academic integrity" encourages instructor use of AI; the nearest type is P59 (instructor use for teaching work), should.
units.anchor: Leverage AI to enhance teaching and learning
units.fit_note: General encouragement with an integrity condition; no specific teaching tasks named.

units.why: "Credit AI-generated materials used in course design, instruction, or assessments" asks instructors to credit AI-made course materials; P48 fits partly, since it asks for credit but not review.
units.anchor: Credit AI-generated materials used in course design, instruction, or assessments
units.fit_note: Asks for crediting only; instructor review of the materials is not mentioned. Says 'credit' rather than disclose and review; the review half of P48 is not stated.
units.resolution_why: unit_stance: A permit, B neutral. "Credit AI-generated materials" is a crediting duty, not a grant of permission to use AI, so neutral. P48 fits partly (credit, no review) as both coders noted.

units.why: "Promote ethical and responsible AI use by modeling best practices and guiding student engagement" asks instructors to model and guide students; closest is P44 (teach effective AI use), though it is about ethical modeling.
units.anchor: modeling best practices and guiding student engagement
units.fit_note: Focuses on ethical modeling and guidance, not on AI as a professional skill. P44 is about professional skill; this passage is about modeling ethical practice, not careers.

units.why: "Clearly state expectations for AI use in your course syllabus, including what is allowed, what requires disclosure, and what is not permitted" asks for a syllabus AI statement: P09.
units.anchor: Clearly state expectations for AI use in your course syllabus

units.why: The same sentence has instructors say "what is allowed" and "what is not permitted", so each instructor sets the rule per course; this separate unit codes that delegation as P04, while the unit above codes the syllabus-statement duty as P09.
units.anchor: what is allowed, what requires disclosure, and what is not permitted
units.policy: Instructors state in the course syllabus what AI use is allowed, what requires disclosure and what is not permitted.
units.fit_note: Fits P04 only partly: the page asks instructors to spell out per-course rules but does not itself say each instructor decides.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this unit; B folded it into the P09 syllabus-statement unit. The same sentence holds two rules: state expectations in the syllabus (P09) and cover what is allowed, what requires disclosure and what is not permitted, which leaves the allow-or-ban decision to the course (P04). Kept as a separate unit because it is the only text that delegates the allow rule, the basis for the delegates stance.

units.why: The Learn tip says "Use AI to support learning and research in ways that align with Tarleton's academic integrity policies", permitting student use on a condition: P02, modality may.
units.anchor: Use AI to support learning and research
units.fit_note: Permission is conditional on alignment with existing academic integrity policies. The permission is conditional on the academic integrity policies, which are not spelled out here.
units.resolution_why: Modality: A should, B may. "Use AI to support learning and research in ways that align with..." grants students conditional permission to use AI (unit_stance permit, P02), the same reading both coders gave the parallel research item "Use AI tools to support idea development", so may.

units.why: "Properly cite AI-generated content when it contributes to academic work, just as with any other source" requires citing AI: P24. P45 does not fit because the sentence treats AI as a source to cite, not as a collaborator.
units.anchor: Properly cite AI-generated content when it contributes to academic work
units.resolution_why: unit_stance: A permit, B neutral. The sentence is a citation duty, not a permission, so neutral. Type P24 agreed.

units.why: "Understand the challenges and limitations of using AI ... including issues of accuracy, bias, and ethical use" tells students to know AI limits; P31 (output may be wrong) is nearest, though it asks for understanding rather than verification.
units.anchor: Understand the challenges and limitations of using AI
units.fit_note: Also names bias and ethical use; it asks for understanding, not for verifying output. Asks students to understand limits (accuracy, bias, ethics); it does not say to verify output.

units.why: Research tip: "Use AI tools to support idea development, content organization, and research design" permits AI in research with oversight; P62 (AI in research) fits, may.
units.anchor: Use AI tools to support idea development, content organization, and research design

units.why: "maintaining human oversight and critical evaluation of all AI-generated content" requires checking AI output in research; P31 fits better than P62 since the point is verification.
units.anchor: human oversight and critical evaluation of all AI-generated content
units.resolution_why: unit_stance: A permit, B neutral. "maintaining human oversight and critical evaluation" is a verification duty, not a permission, so neutral. P31 agreed.

units.why: "Choose AI platforms that uphold strong data privacy standards and do not use inputted data to train publicly accessible models" tells researchers to prefer privacy-protecting tools: P50.
units.anchor: Choose AI platforms that uphold strong data privacy standards

units.why: "include appropriate disclosures in informed consent documents" is a research-participant rule about AI risks: P62 (AI in research).
units.anchor: include appropriate disclosures in informed consent documents

units.why: "Understand and comply with publisher requirements regarding the use and disclosure of AI in submitted work" defers to venue rules, exactly P62.
units.anchor: comply with publisher requirements regarding the use and disclosure of AI
units.resolution_why: Phase: A during-work, B general. The tip tells researchers or staff what to do while carrying out their research or work with AI, so during-work. Modality: A should, B must. The page labels these "Quick Guidelines" and the research items are recommendations; the sentence also says "Understand", so should. Type agreed.

units.why: "Acknowledge how AI may affect the explanation, reproduction, and validity of your research findings" asks researchers to acknowledge AI effects on research integrity: P62, with a disclosure flavor.
units.anchor: Acknowledge how AI may affect the explanation, reproduction, and validity
units.resolution_why: Phase: A during-work, B general. The tip tells researchers or staff what to do while carrying out their research or work with AI, so during-work. Type agreed.

units.why: "Acquire and use training data in accordance with consent, privacy laws, and institutional review board (IRB) standards" requires legal and IRB compliance in research: P62 (defers to IRB rules); P77 is less specific.
units.anchor: in accordance with consent, privacy laws, and institutional review board (IRB) standards
units.fit_note: Also requires compliance with privacy law (P77) in addition to IRB deference.
units.resolution_why: Phase: A during-work, B general. The tip tells researchers or staff what to do while carrying out their research or work with AI, so during-work. Type agreed.

units.why: Work tip: "Leverage AI to enhance efficiency and decision-making, improving workflows and service delivery across departments" encourages staff operational use: P76.
units.anchor: Leverage AI to enhance efficiency and decision-making
units.resolution_why: Phase: A during-work, B general. The tip tells researchers or staff what to do while carrying out their research or work with AI, so during-work. Type agreed.

units.why: "Prioritize data privacy and security when using AI tools, ensuring compliance with university policies and applicable regulations" asks staff to protect data and comply; P50 is primary, with compliance noted.
units.anchor: Prioritize data privacy and security when using AI tools
units.fit_note: Also requires compliance with university policies and regulations (P77).
units.resolution_why: Phase: A during-work, B general. The tip tells researchers or staff what to do while carrying out their research or work with AI, so during-work. Type agreed.

units.why: "Stay informed about evolving AI technologies, best practices, and ethical considerations" is a duty to keep current: P102.
units.anchor: Stay informed about evolving AI technologies, best practices, and ethical considerations

notes: Single included document (university layer). Linked Provost task force report and syllabus guidance pages were not collected; the course layer is deferred. Navigation and link lists are not coded (coder A unit for the link title "Center of Educational Excellence: AI Resources" dropped: it states no policy). Reconciled from coders A and B.
